entity_ranked_evidence.title: India protest movement holds capital sit-in as police crack down on demonstrators - San Francisco Chronicle
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: NEW DELHI (AP) — Thousands of young protesters were camped on the streets of India’s capital New Delhi on Thursday, defying new restrictions in the latest show of strength for a movement that has become one of the biggest challenges to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government. India’s “Cockroach” protests began more than a month ago over alleged leaks in some of the country’s most competitive entrance exams for medical colleges and government jobs. Thursday’s demonstrations at Jantar Mantar, a designated protest site in New Delhi, followed overnight clashes in which police used tear gas and batons to disperse crowds, the second such confrontation this week. The issue of exam leaks has become a powerful symbol of frustration for millions of young Indians. For many young Indians, the protests have become one of the few visible expressions of dissent in a country where demonstrations against Modi’s government have led to a broader crackdown on activists, opposition figures and public protests.

entity_ranked_evidence.title: College Democrats’ Jewish caucus demands apology for group’s hosting of Hasan Piker - The Times of Israel
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: # College Democrats’ Jewish caucus demands apology for group’s hosting of Hasan Piker. ## Jews in campus group call far-left commentator's appearance a 'direct threat to Jewish safety and inclusion,' say organizers blocked protest walkout by citing 'security concerns'. The Jewish caucus of the College Democrats of America on Tuesday condemned the organization for hosting the far-left, anti-Zionist streamer Hasan Piker at the group’s national convention over the weekend. The College Democrats of America is a campus activist group that says it has more than 100,000 members at colleges across the US. “The normalization of Piker and his rhetoric in CDA-sanctioned programming is a direct threat to Jewish safety and inclusion within the College Democrats community,” the statement said. A member of the caucus, who asked to remain anonymous, told The Times of Israel that members only heard of Piker’s appearance through a surprise announcement on social media, after they had already traveled to the convention.

entity_ranked_evidence.title: EMS Apprenticeships as a Disaster-Driven Workforce Pipeline - jems.com
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: # EMS Apprenticeships as a Disaster-Driven Workforce Pipeline. Emergency medical services (EMS) systems in the United States struggle to meet workforce demands due to unprecedented stress on traditional training pipelines. As a proven model for workforce training, apprenticeships are well-suited to meet the needs of the EMS workforce. This article examines how EMS apprenticeship programs, such as the one developed by Lansing Community College (LCC), offer a scalable workforce pipeline solution. Using the Lansing program as a case study, this article illustrates how partnerships between community colleges, public safety agencies, and workforce organizations can expand the EMS workforce during periods of increased demand. First responders were similarly afflicted by stress and overload during the COVID-19 pandemic.2 However, the confluence of increasing disasters, such as wildfires in Los Angeles and Hawaii, and flooding in Texas, coupled with ongoing workforce instability, created a critical need for innovative training solutions that build resilience and meet demands in real time.3.
